answer_1.quote: In this work, we propose to combine the efficiency and quantification of automated methods with the flexibility of human evaluators... our approach works as follows: We generate a set of outputs for two different prompts or models and then automatically extract descriptions of the differences between the sets of texts.
datasets: opinion dataset from Shu et al.
answer_1.outputs: longer LLM output texts such as stories, emails, movie reviews, and summaries

answer_2.quote: Automated metrics, such as accuracy or BLEU scores, are fast to compute and allow for easy quantitative comparisons.

answer_3.quote: We evaluate two versions of the open source model Llama 3.1 (8B and 70B) as well as the commercial GPT-4o via the OpenAI API... Please identify words or phrases that are systematically different between the texts of the two groups.
methods: direct comparison of word/phrase differences between two groups of texts

answer_4.quote: We ran a user study to evaluate how difficult it is for users to identify significant differences and if they can leverage token patterns. We asked participants (n = 50) on the crowdworking platform Prolific to identify differences between two groups of LLM-generated texts.
answer_4.guideline: Participants were asked to describe the differences in free-text form, with or without a token pattern for the target difference being shown to them. They were told there could be no, one, or multiple differences.
